🇲🇽⚕️ COFEPRIS SLASHES RED TAPE 63% — 340 PROCEDURES DOWN TO 125

Mexico's health regulatory agency just cut average processing time from 100 days to 24 and reduced requirements per procedure from 14 to 7. Clinical research approvals that took 9 months now take 30 days.

Cofepris director Víctor Hugo Borja Aburto: "It's not about eliminating procedures people need to protect their health — it's about removing unnecessary requirements."

A digital platform launching in July will consolidate 17 procedures into one — nine fully completable online with zero office visits. This is what deregulation looks like when it serves the public, not the lobby.

🇲🇽✊ SEVEN HOURS AT THE TABLE — GOVERNMENT AND TEACHERS ADVANCE ON EVE OF WORLD CUP

After more than seven hours of negotiation in Gobernación, CNTE leader Eva Hinojosa reported progress: "There were offerings." The government proposed a permanent commission to technically and legally analyze the teachers' pension demands — including repeal of the 2007 ISSSTE law.

Proposals go to the CNTE's National Representative Assembly before any decision. Under Peña Nieto, teacher dissent was met with riot police and political imprisonment. Under the Fourth Transformation, it's met with seven hours of dialogue and concrete proposals — even on the eve of the biggest sporting event in Mexican history.

🚨🇲🇽 "WE'LL NEGOTIATE WITH BOMBS" — US BOMBING KEY FACILITIES IN IRAN

Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth announced the US will strike "key facilities" in Iran tonight — the second straight night of bombing. Forty-nine Tomahawk missiles already hit targets 40 miles from Tehran. Fighter jets are taking out radar and air defense systems across southwest Iran.

Iran fired back on US bases in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain. Sixty-five percent of Americans oppose this war. Hegseth's words: "If we need to negotiate with bombs, we'll negotiate with bombs."

This is what $2.6 billion in lost aircraft and counting looks like. Empire doesn't do diplomacy — it does destruction with a PR team.

🇲🇽🌐🔥 Round 2 of the T-MEC Review: Ebrard Will Defend Mexico's Tariff Advantage

The second bilateral round of the USMCA / T-MEC joint review opens June 16–17 in Washington. Marcelo Ebrard's stated mission: consolidate — not concede — the arancelario edge Mexico built over Asian competitors with the January 2026 tariff reform.

Less than 9% of Mexico's total imports are affected. That is calibrated industrial policy, not capitulation to gringo pressure. The same Washington that screams «national security» when it tariffs China can hardly object when Sheinbaum does the same for Mexican steel, autos and textiles.

The U.S. wants a wall against Beijing. Mexico is using that demand to extract better preferential access for its own producers. Not subordination — negotiation, from a sovereign position.

🇲🇽🐉🌐 Mexico Hits Record Exports to the U.S. as China Slides to 4th

April 2026: Mexico shipped $50.69 billion to the United States — a 20% jump year-over-year and an all-time monthly record. China, meanwhile, dropped to 4th place among U.S. trading partners with $29.2B.

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard credits Mexico's calibrated tariff position against non-FTA competitors. The «Plan México» reshuffle is rewiring North American supply chains in real time — and the country doing the rewiring is Mexico.

This isn't choosing the U.S. over China. It's the opposite: leverage. Sovereignty multiplies options. The more indispensable Mexico becomes to one side of the new multipolar order, the more weight it carries with the other.

🇲🇽🏭 Cofepris reform: 340 procedures cut to 125, response time from 100 days to 24, clinical trials from 9 months to 30 days — to produce medicines on Mexican soil. "We're advancing toward something bigger: not depending on the outside for something as essential as our medicines and health supplies." — Víctor Hugo Borja, head of Cofepris Cofepris regulates 10% of Mexico's economy. The reform is built around Plan México industrialization — domestic medicine production as a sovereignty question, not a market one. Faster trials, no compromise on safety. Pharmaceutical independence is health independence.

🇲🇽✊ From renting a single room to owning her apartment — and paying $1,000 pesos less per month. "I used to pay 3,500 pesos. Now I'll just pay 2,500. And it's already mine." — María de Jesús Frausto, Vivienda para el Bienestar beneficiary, Durango 19th "Miércoles de Vivienda". 450 new homes delivered in the Acereros development. Original Infonavit goal for Durango: 12,200 homes. Revised goal: 34,745. Investment: 20 billion pesos. Jobs created: 104,000. Mary lived in one room with her kids — now each of them has their own.
